## §3.1.1–3.1.2: The Principle of Inversion & The $2 \times 2$ Korporator {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">LEVEL III OF KONSTITUTIONSSTAMMBAUM &amp; STRATUM D (SM, PP. 42–46, EQS. 10–11)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
### Breaking Monadic Isolation: *Prinzip der Inversion*
* Chapter 2 proved **Spaltbarkeit**: every history-dependent homogeneous Syntrix ($\homsyntrix$) factors into a pyramidal core and an interaction fragment ($\overline{T}_{\mathrm{frag}} \circ \overline{T}_{\mathrm{pyr}}$).
* In §3.1 (SM, p. 42), Heim invokes the **Principle of Inversion**: if complex systems can be split into elementary pyramidal syntrices, then nature must possess the exact inverse synthetic functor—the **Korporator**—binding autonomous Syntrices $S_a, S_b$ into an encompassing $S_c$.

::: {.thm-box .fragment}
**Dual-Tier Action (*Duale Wirkung*, SM Eqs. 10–11):**
$$
\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \left\{ K_m \quad C_m \right\} \widetilde{\mathrm{b}},\; \overline{|CS|}_\gamma,\; \widetilde{\mathrm{c}} \quad \lor \quad (\underline{f, m}), \left\{ K_s \quad C_s \right\}, (\underline{\varphi, \mu}),\; \overline{|AS|}_\gamma,\; (\underline{G, N}) \tag{SM-10}
$$
$$
\langle\langle f \widetilde{a} \rangle m \rangle \left\{ \begin{matrix} K_s & C_s \\ K_m & C_m \end{matrix} \right\} \langle\langle \varphi \widetilde{b} \rangle \mu \rangle,\; \overline{|CS_c|}_\gamma,\; \langle\langle G \widetilde{c} \rangle N \rangle \tag{SM-11}
$$

1. **Lower Tier (*Metrophorkorporation*):** Combines static carrier cores $\widetilde{a}_a$ ($p$ elements) and $\widetilde{a}_b$ ($q$ elements) via **Koppelung ($K_m$)** or **Komposition ($C_m$)**.
2. **Upper Tier (*Synkolative Korporation*):** Combines dynamic generative modules via **Cross-Modulation ($K_s$)** or **Parallel Sum ($C_s$)** with arity $M_c = \Phi(m_a, m_b)$.
:::

:::

## §3.1.3–3.1.4: *Eindeutigkeitssatz*, *Nullsyntrix* & Decompositions {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: UNAMBIGUITY &amp; BASIS DECOMPOSITIONS (SM-11a, 11b, 11c)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Heim's *Eindeutigkeitssatz* (Unambiguity Theorem, SM, p. 50):**
> *"Ein Korporator ist dann und nur dann eindeutig, wenn er mindestens eine synkolative und mindestens eine metrophorische Verknüpfungsregel enthält."*

* **Totalkorporationen:** Employ strictly one rule type ($K$ or $C$) on a single active tier; generically ambiguous (*zweideutig*, SM, p. 48) because the other tier is left underdetermined.
* **Partielle Korporationen:** Mix coupling and composition rules across both tiers.
* **Korporatorklassen ($\kappa = 1 \dots 4$):** $\sum_{\kappa=1}^4 \binom{4}{\kappa} = 15$ non-empty classes.
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment}
**The *Nullsyntrix* ($\nullsyntrix$, SM Eq. 11a, p. 51):**
$$
\widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \{ \} \widetilde{\mathrm{b}},\; \overline{||},\; \nullsyntrix \quad \lor \quad \nullsyntrix \equiv \langle \bar{\mathrm{f}} \widetilde{\mathrm{c}} \bar{\mathrm{m}} \rangle \tag{SM-11a}
$$
Possesses an empty Synkolator $\bar{f}$ ($F_\gamma = \emptyset\;\forall \gamma \ge 1$), acting as the terminal boundary object closing deductive chains and Metrophoric Cycles.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

<div class="video-container">
  <video autoplay data-autoplay loop muted playsinline src="media/Ch3_Act2_Eindeutigkeit_Decomp.mp4" style="max-height:260px;"></video>
  <div class="video-caption">Manim Act II: The Eindeutigkeitssatz, Nullsyntrix &amp; 4 Pyramidal Basis Gates</div>
</div>

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**First & Second Decomposition Theorems (SM Eqs. 11b, 11c, pp. 53–54):**

1. **First Decomposition Theorem (SM-11b):** Every homogeneous syntrix ($\homsyntrix$) decomposes via synkolative contractions $D_s$ into a sequential chain of pyramidal syntrices terminating in $\nullsyntrix$:
$$
\langle\langle \mathrm{f} \widetilde{\mathrm{a}} \rangle \mathrm{m} \rangle,\; \overline{||},\; \widetilde{\mathrm{a}}_1 \{ \}_1 \widetilde{\mathrm{a}}_2 \{ \}_2 \dots \{ \}_{k-1} \widetilde{\mathrm{a}}_k \{ \}_k \dots \{ \}_{L-1} \nullsyntrix \tag{SM-11b}
$$
2. **Second Decomposition Theorem (SM-11c):** Every pyramidal syntrix decomposes into the **4 elementary pyramidal structures**:
$$
\syntrix,\; \overline{||},\; \syntrix_{(1)} \{ \} \syntrix_{(2)} \{ \} \syntrix_{(3)} \{ \} \syntrix_{(4)} \tag{SM-11c}
$$
:::

:::

::::

::: {.notes}
Section 3.1.3 establishes Heim's Eindeutigkeitssatz: a corporate operation is uniquely determined if and only if it specifies at least one metrophoric rule and at least one synkolative rule. Section 3.1.4 states the two foundational decomposition theorems: every homogeneous syntrix unravels into a chain of pyramidal syntrices terminating at the Nullsyntrix, and every pyramidal syntrix decomposes into the 4 elementary structures.
:::

## §3.1.5 & §3.2.1–3.2.2: Category $\mathbf{Syn}$ & Zero Object $0_{\mathbf{Syn}}$ {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: CARRIER FUNCTOR (DEF. 3.2), CATEGORY SYN (DEF. 3.3) &amp; ZERO OBJECT (PROP. 3.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="52%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definitions 3.1–3.3: Carrier Functor $\mathfrak{R}$ & Category $\mathbf{Syn}$**
The **Carrier Realization Functor** $\mathfrak{R} \colon \Ctx \to \FinBan$ maps $U \mapsto P^U$ and $\alpha \mapsto \alpha_P$.
An object in $\mathbf{Syn}$ is a quadruple $\mathcal{S} \coloneqq (U, \mathbf{F}, \theta, \iota)$ where:

* $\mathbf{F} = \{F_\gamma\}_{\gamma \ge 0} \in \operatorname{Obj}(\FinBan^{\mathbb{N}_0})$ is a graded sequence of finite-dimensional Banach spaces;
* $\iota \colon F_0 \xrightarrow{\sim} P^U$ is an isometric identification of the grade-$0$ syndrome with the context carrier;
* $\theta_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma} \colon \Osyn(\vec{\gamma};\gamma) \otpi \bigotimes F_{\gamma_i} \to F_\gamma$ are contractive operadic evaluations.

Morphisms $\Phi = (h, (\Phi_\gamma)_{\gamma\ge 0}) \colon \mathcal{S}_a \to \mathcal{S}_b$ intertwine $\iota$ and $\theta$:
$$
\iota_b \circ \Phi_0 = h_P \circ \iota_a, \qquad \Phi_\gamma \circ \theta_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma}^a = \theta_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma}^b \circ \big(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{O}} \otpi \bigotimes \Phi_{\gamma_i}\big)
$$
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment}
**Proposition 3.1 (Three Structural Distributions in Conflexive Architectures):**
Every conflexive network $\konflexiv$ (SM Eqs. 12–13a) is characterized by: (1) the lengths $k_i - 1$ of its **Syntropoden**, (2) the locations of its **Konflexionsfelder**, and (3) the synkolation branches above those fields.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

<div class="video-container">
  <video autoplay data-autoplay loop muted playsinline src="media/Ch3_Act3_Category_Syn_Zero.mp4" style="max-height:265px;"></video>
  <div class="video-caption">Manim Act III: Commutative Intertwining in Syn &amp; Universal Zero Object 0_Syn</div>
</div>

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Proposition 3.2: The Zero Object $0_{\mathbf{Syn}}$ (*Nullsyntrix*)**
$$
0_{\mathbf{Syn}} \;\coloneqq\; \big(0_{\mathbf{Ctx}},\, \{0\}_{\gamma \ge 0},\, 0,\, \operatorname{id}_{\{0\}}\big)
$$
is both **initial and terminal** in $\mathbf{Syn}$:
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Syn}}(0_{\mathbf{Syn}}, \mathcal{S}) = \{!\}, \qquad \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Syn}}(\mathcal{S}, 0_{\mathbf{Syn}}) = \{!\}
$$
providing the exact categorical realization of Heim's *Nullsyntrix* ($\nullsyntrix$).
:::

:::

::::

::: {.notes}
In Stratum A, we unite the context carriers of Chapter 1 with the colored operad algebras of Chapter 2 into the category Syn. Proposition 3.2 proves that the trivial syntrix 0_Syn is both initial and terminal in Syn, giving a rigorous universal-property definition to Heim's Nullsyntrix.
:::

## §3.2.3: Carrier Coproducts ($C_m$) vs. Span Pushouts ($K_m$) {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: GEOMETRY OF KONZENTER &amp; EXZENTER (DEF. 3.4, FIGS. 3.1–3.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.carnap-box}
**Carnap 3.1: Intersubjective Constitution & OSR via Span Pushouts**
Following Carnap (*Aufbau* §§146–148) and Steven French's *Ontic Structural Realism* (2014), binding two $p$- and $q$-dimensional carriers across $\lambda$ shared channels is **not** a $(p \cdot q)$ tensor product, but a **categorical span pushout** in $\FinBan$:

1. **Composition ($C_m$ — *Konzenter*):** $\ell^1$-coproduct $P_a \oplus_1 P_b$ ($\dim = p + q$).
2. **Coupling ($K_m$ — *Exzenter*):** Given span $P_a \xleftarrow{\phi_a} R_\phi \xrightarrow{\phi_b} P_b$ with difference map $\delta_\phi(r) \coloneqq (\phi_a(r), -\phi_b(r))$:
$$
P_a \boxplusphi P_b \;\coloneqq\; \frac{P_a \oplus_1 P_b}{\Im(\delta_\phi)}, \qquad \dim(P_a \boxplusphi P_b) = p + q - \lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}
$$
where $\lambda_{\mathrm{eff}} \coloneqq \rank(\delta_\phi) = \dim R_\phi - \dim(\ker\phi_a \cap \ker\phi_b)$, equipped with quotient norm $\|[(x,y)]\|_q = \inf_{r\in R_\phi}(\|x - \phi_a(r)\|_{P_a} + \|y + \phi_b(r)\|_{P_b})$.
:::

Why does an Exzenter coupling have dimension p + q - lambda rather than p * q? Because identifying lambda shared channels between two observers is a categorical span pushout P_a boxplus_phi P_b = (P_a oplus_1 P_b) / Im(delta_phi). In Stage III of our Running Example, coupling two 6-dimensional polarimeters across a 3D shared polarization channel yields a 9D pushout whose second exterior power has dimension C(9,2) = 36—the exact carrier capacity of the Chapter 9 Hermetry matrix!
:::

## §3.2.4 & §3.3.1: *Konflektorknoten*, Module Lifts & Determinacy {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM A/B: MODULE LIFTS (DEF. 3.5, PROP. 3.3), VALENCY (DEF. 3.6) &amp; DETERMINACY (THM. 3.4)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Def. 3.5 & Prop. 3.3: Synkolative Module Lifts ($C_s, K_s$)**
1. **Parallel Composition Module ($C_s$):**
$$
\big(\mathbf{F}^{C_s}\big)_\gamma \coloneqq F_\gamma^a \oplus_1 F_\gamma^b, \qquad \theta^{C_s}(f \otimes \vec{u}) = \big(\theta^a(f \otimes \vec{x}),\, \theta^b(f \otimes \vec{y})\big)
$$
2. **Cross-Modulating Coupling Module ($K_s$):**
$$
\big(\mathbf{F}^{K_s}\big)_\gamma \coloneqq \bigoplus_{\alpha+\beta=\gamma}^{\ell^1} F_\alpha^a \otpi F_\beta^b, \qquad \theta^{K_s} \coloneqq (\theta^a \otpi \theta^b) \circ \tau_m \circ (\Delta_{\vec{\gamma};\gamma} \otpi \operatorname{id})
$$
or universally via the amalgamated operadic coproduct $\mathbf{F}^a \star_{\Osyn}^{R_\phi} \mathbf{F}^b \coloneqq \operatorname{Free}_{\Osyn}(P^{U_c}) / \mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{rel}}^{a,b}$.
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Def. 3.7 & Theorem 3.4: 3-Level Corporate Construction Determinacy**
* **Level I (Rule Selection):** $r \subseteq \{K_s, C_s, K_m, C_m\}$.
* **Level II (Specification Datum):** $\Sigma_r = (r, \Sigma_m, \Sigma_s, \Phi, \Gamma, \mathsf{Comp})$.
* **Level III (Universal Determinacy):** $\Kor_{r, \Sigma_r}(\mathcal{S}_a, \mathcal{S}_b) = \mathcal{S}_c \in \operatorname{Obj}(\mathbf{Syn})$ is **uniquely determined up to unique isometric isomorphism**.
:::

:::

## §3.3.2: 4D Tesseract of the 15 Corporate Classes {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: COMBINATORIAL PARTITION (DEF. 3.8, PROPS. 3.5–3.6, FIG. 3.5)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="47%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Def. 3.8 & Props. 3.5–3.6: The 9 Mixed vs. 6 Pure Partition**
Let $\mathsf{Met} \coloneqq \{K_m, C_m\}$ and $\mathsf{Synk} \coloneqq \{K_s, C_s\}$. The $2^4 - 1 = 15$ non-empty subsets $r \subseteq \{K_s, C_s, K_m, C_m\}$ partition by rank $\kappa = |r|$:

| Rank $\kappa$ | $\binom{4}{\kappa}$ | **Mixed ($r\cap\mathsf{Met}\ne\emptyset \wedge r\cap\mathsf{Synk}\ne\emptyset$)** | **Pure ($r\subseteq\mathsf{Met}$ or $r\subseteq\mathsf{Synk}$)** |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| $\kappa = 4$ | $1$ | **$1$** ($\{K_s, C_s, K_m, C_m\}$) | $0$ |
| $\kappa = 3$ | $4$ | **$4$** (All 4 Triads) | $0$ |
| $\kappa = 2$ | $6$ | **$4$** (Cross-Tier Pairs) | **$2$** ($\{K_m,C_m\}, \{K_s,C_s\}$) |
| $\kappa = 1$ | $4$ | $0$ | **$4$** (Singletons) |
| **Total** | **15** | **9 Mixed (Determinate)** | **6 Pure (Underdetermined)** |
:::

## §3.3.3–3.3.4: Basis Generation & Homogeneous Decomposition {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B/C: PYRAMIDAL BASIS (PROP. 3.7) &amp; HOMOGENEOUS DECOMPOSITION (THMS. 3.8–3.10)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Assumption 3.1, Prop. 3.7 & Theorem 3.8: Corporate Decompositions**

1. **Pyramidal Basis Generation (Prop. 3.7):** Under $\Opyr = \langle E_{(1)}, E_{(2)}, E_{(3)}, E_{(4)} \rangle$, every finite pyramidal syntrix algebra belongs to the corporate colimit closure:
$$
\mathcal{S} \in \operatorname{Colim}\!\big\langle \mathcal{S}_{(1)},\; \mathcal{S}_{(2)},\; \mathcal{S}_{(3)},\; \mathcal{S}_{(4)} \big\rangle_{\Kor}
$$
2. **Conditional Corporate Decomposition (Thm. 3.8, SM Eq. 11b):** Under a well-founded complexity functional $\mu \colon \operatorname{Obj}(\mathbf{Syn}_{\mathrm{hom}}) \to \mathbb{N}$ with $\mu(D_s(\mathcal{S})) < \mu(\mathcal{S})$ and $\mu(\mathcal{S}) = 0 \iff \mathcal{S} \cong 0_{\mathbf{Syn}}$, every homogeneous syntrix decomposes in $L < \infty$ steps:
$$
\mathcal{S} \;\cong\; \Kor_{r_{L-1}}\!\Big( \dots \Kor_{r_1}(\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2) \dots,\; \mathcal{S}_L \Big)
$$
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Prop. 3.9 (*Enthomogenisierende Dekomposition*) & Thm. 3.10:**
* Contra-operative decoupling removes the shared first syndrome ($\mu = \dim F_1$) from higher homogeneous fragments, so extracted pyramidal syntrices begin at $\gamma = 2$.
* Under purely compositive corporate operators, syndrome populations satisfy:
$$
n_H - \mu \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^p n_j \tag{Eq. 3.16}
$$
:::

## §3.3.5: Syntropod Networks, Conflexivity & 21-Branch Fan-Out {.smaller}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: COLIMIT TREES (DEF. 3.12, PROP. 3.13) &amp; PSEUDOEXZENTER FAN-OUT (THM. 3.11)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="47%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Defs. 3.10–3.12 & Prop. 3.13: Syntropod Trees & Conflexivity Index**
* The $i$-th **Syntropode** of length $k_i - 1$ is the truncated submodule $\tau_{\le k_i - 1}(\mathcal{S}_i)$.
* Over a decorated corporate interaction tree $G_{\mathcal{S}} = (V, E_C \sqcup E_K, \Sigma)$ on $N = |V|$ Syntropoden with $\varepsilon \coloneqq |E_K|$ Exzenter edges, deleting $E_K$ yields a Concentric Forest with:
$$
\ConfIndex(G_{\mathcal{S}}) \;\coloneqq\; k(V, E_C) \;=\; |E_K| + 1 \;=\; \varepsilon + 1
$$
and global colimit $\konflexiv \cong \varinjlim_{\mathsf{Tree}_{\Kor}(G_{\mathcal{S}})} D$.
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment}
**Theorem 3.11: Pseudoexcentric Branch Fan-Out ($\frac{1}{2}N(N+1)$)**
Connecting $N \ge 2$ disjoint Metrophor origins via a *Pseudoexzenter* (SM, pp. 57, 61) fans out into $N$ pure single-metrophor branches plus $\binom{N}{2}$ mixed pairwise branches:
$$
N_{\mathrm{branches}} \;=\; N + \binom{N}{2} \;=\; \mathbf{\frac{1}{2}N(N+1)}
$$
For $N = 6$, this yields $\frac{1}{2}(6)(7) = \mathbf{21}$ branches (matching the 21 symmetric potentials of the 36-component Hermetry matrix!).
:::

**Carnap 3.2: Humphreys's Fusion Emergence in Conflexion Fields (1997)**
1. **Token Absorption:** Quotienting by $\Im(\delta_\phi)$ erases separate identity on $\lambda$ channels ($p+q \to p+q-\lambda$).
2. **Topological Novelty:** Trivial local chains glue across $R_\phi$ into global cycles in $\Im(\partial_*) \subset H_{\gamma+1}(\mathcal{S}_c)$.

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Def. 3.14 & Theorem 3.15: $\DKor(\mathbf{Syn})$ & Mayer–Vietoris Sequence**
* In $\DKor(\mathbf{Syn})$, horizontal 1-cells are corporate spans $\mathfrak{K} = (\mathcal{S}_\phi, \phi_a, \phi_b, \Sigma_r)$ composed via fiber pullbacks $R_{\phi_1} \times_{P_b} R_{\phi_2}$.
* Every Exzenter pushout induces a short exact sequence of chain complexes $0 \to C_\bullet(\mathcal{S}_\phi) \xrightarrow{\delta_\phi} C_\bullet(\mathcal{S}_a)\oplus_1 C_\bullet(\mathcal{S}_b) \xrightarrow{\pi_{\boxplus}} C_\bullet(\mathcal{S}_c) \to 0$, yielding:
$$
\cdots \to H_{\gamma+1}(\mathcal{S}_a)\oplus H_{\gamma+1}(\mathcal{S}_b) \xrightarrow{\pi_*} H_{\gamma+1}(\mathcal{S}_c) \xrightarrow{\partial_*} H_\gamma(\mathcal{S}_\phi) \xrightarrow{\delta_{\phi *}} H_\gamma(\mathcal{S}_a)\oplus H_\gamma(\mathcal{S}_b) \to \cdots
$$
:::

### Compile-Ready Lean 4 Blueprint (`StratumA.Corporations`, App. C)

<div class="lean-code-card">
<pre style="margin:0;"><code>import Mathlib
namespace Syntrometrie.StratumA.Corporations

inductive CorporateRule where
  | Km | Cm | Ks | Cs
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

def IsMixedSelection (r : Finset CorporateRule) : Bool :=
  (CorporateRule.Km ∈ r || CorporateRule.Cm ∈ r) &&
  (CorporateRule.Ks ∈ r || CorporateRule.Cs ∈ r)

def pushoutCarrierDim (p q lambda_eff : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (p + q) - lambda_eff

theorem pushoutCarrierDim_uncoupled (p q : ℕ) :
    pushoutCarrierDim p q 0 = p + q := rfl

end Syntrometrie.StratumA.Corporations</code></pre>
</div>

:::

<!-- UNIFIED RESILIENT JAVASCRIPT ENGINE FOR ALL 8 CHAPTER 3 WIDGETS -->
<script>
window.comb3 = function(n, k) {
  if (k < 0 || k > n) return 0;
  if (k === 0 || k === n) return 1;
  let r = 1;
  for (let i = 1; i <= k; i++) r = r * (n - i + 1) / i;
  return Math.round(r);
};

// WIDGET 1: §3.1.2 Metrophorkorporation Coupling Mode Explorer
window.updateMetCorp = function() {
  const elP = document.getElementById('mc-p');
  if (!elP) return;
  let p = parseInt(elP.value);
  let q = parseInt(document.getElementById('mc-q').value);
  let lamIn = document.getElementById('mc-lam');
  let maxL = Math.min(p, q);
  lamIn.max = maxL;
  let lam = Math.min(maxL, parseInt(lamIn.value));
  lamIn.value = lam;

  document.getElementById('mc-p-val').innerText = p;
  document.getElementById('mc-q-val').innerText = q;
  document.getElementById('mc-lam-val').innerText = lam;

  let uncoupled = p + q;
  let nonComb = (p + q - 2 * lam) + lam; // p + q - lam
  let combCount = p * lam * q;

  const box = document.getElementById('mc-readout');
  if (box) {
    box.innerHTML =
      `<b>1. Uncoupled Composition (C_m):</b> p + q = <b style="color:#82aaff;">${uncoupled}</b> independent channels<br>` +
      `<b>2. Non-Combinatorial Coupling (K_m Pushout, SM p. 43):</b> (p + q - 2λ) + λ = p + q - λ = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${nonComb}</b><br>` +
      `<b>3. Combinatorial Coupling (Heim SM p. 44):</b> Z_comb = p · λ · q = <b style="color:#20B2AA;">${combCount}</b> coupled pairs`;
  }
};

// WIDGET 2: §3.2.3 Span Pushout & Stage III Polarimeter Lab
window.updatePushoutLab = function() {
  const elP = document.getElementById('po-p');
  if (!elP) return;
  let p = parseInt(elP.value);
  let q = parseInt(document.getElementById('po-q').value);
  let lamInput = document.getElementById('po-lam');
  let maxLam = Math.min(p, q);
  lamInput.max = maxLam;
  let lam = Math.min(maxLam, parseInt(lamInput.value));
  lamInput.value = lam;

  document.getElementById('po-p-val').innerText = p;
  document.getElementById('po-q-val').innerText = q;
  document.getElementById('po-lam-val').innerText = lam;

  let dimCoprod = p + q;
  let dimPushout = p + q - lam;
  let ext2 = window.comb3(dimPushout, 2);

  // Update SVG Orbital Circles
  let frac = maxLam > 0 ? (lam / maxLam) : 0;
  let sep = 42 * (1.0 - 0.85 * frac);
  const c1 = document.getElementById('po-c1');
  const c2 = document.getElementById('po-c2');
  const knot = document.getElementById('po-knot');
  const kTxt = document.getElementById('po-knot-txt');
  if (c1 && c2 && knot && kTxt) {
    c1.setAttribute('cx', (105 - sep).toFixed(1));
    c2.setAttribute('cx', (105 + sep).toFixed(1));
    knot.setAttribute('r', (lam === 0 ? 0 : 7 + lam * 2.2).toFixed(1));
    kTxt.setAttribute('opacity', lam === 0 ? '0' : '1');
  }

  let note = "";
  if (p === 6 && q === 6 && lam === 3) {
    note = `<br><span style="color:#FFD700;">★ STAGE III POLARIMETER MATCH: dim(P_c) = 9 ⇒ dim Λ²(ℝ⁹) = C(9,2) = <b>36</b> (Exact Ch. 9 Hermetry Capacity!)</span>`;
  } else if (lam === 0) {
    note = `<br><span style="color:#82aaff;">★ UNCOUPLED KONZENTER LIMIT (λ = 0): P_a ⊞₀ P_b ≅ P_a ⊕₁ P_b (dim = ${dimCoprod})</span>`;
  } else if (lam === p && p === q) {
    note = `<br><span style="color:#20B2AA;">★ FULL IDENTIFICATION LIMIT (λ = p = q): P_a ⊞_id P_a ≅ P_a (dim = ${p}, zero channel inflation)</span>`;
  }

  document.getElementById('po-lab-readout').innerHTML =
    `<b>Coproduct Dim (C_m):</b> p + q = ${dimCoprod}  |  <b>Span Pushout Dim (K_m):</b> p + q - λ_eff = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${dimPushout}</b><br>` +
    `<b>Coincidence Module F₁^c = Λ²(P_c):</b> C(${dimPushout}, 2) = <b style="color:#20B2AA;">${ext2}</b>` + note;
};

window.setPoPreset = function(p, q, lam) {
  document.getElementById('po-p').value = p;
  document.getElementById('po-q').value = q;
  document.getElementById('po-lam').max = Math.min(p, q);
  document.getElementById('po-lam').value = lam;
  window.updatePushoutLab();
};

// WIDGET 3: §3.2.4 Konflektorknoten & Factual Valency Lab
window.updateKonflektorLab = function() {
  const elChi = document.getElementById('kf-chi');
  if (!elChi) return;
  let chi = parseFloat(elChi.value);
  let th = parseFloat(document.getElementById('kf-th').value);
  let r = parseInt(document.getElementById('kf-r').value);
  let nIn = document.getElementById('kf-n');
  nIn.max = r;
  let n = Math.min(r, parseInt(nIn.value));
  nIn.value = n;

  document.getElementById('kf-r-val').innerText = r;
  document.getElementById('kf-n-val').innerText = n;

  let valFact = r - n + 1;
  let boundStatus = chi > th
    ? `<span style="color:#20B2AA;"><b>✓ KONFLEKTORKNOTEN ACTIVE (χ=${chi.toFixed(2)} > θ=${th.toFixed(2)}):</b> Quotient relation δ_φ(r) = (φ_a r, -φ_b r) = 0 binds c_l = (a₁, φ_l, b₂)!</span>`
    : `<span style="color:#ff6b81;"><b>✗ BELOW THRESHOLD (χ=${chi.toFixed(2)} ≤ θ=${th.toFixed(2)}):</b> Channels remain uncoupled in P_a ⊕₁ P_b.</span>`;

  const box = document.getElementById('kf-readout');
  if (box) {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = chi > th ? "#20B2AA" : "#DC143C";
    box.innerHTML = `${boundStatus}<br><b>Def. 3.6 (Pseudovalenz r = ${r} with n = ${n} identical inputs):</b> Factual Valency Val_fact = r - n + 1 = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${valFact}</b>`;
  }
};

// WIDGET 4: §3.3.2 2x2 Korporator Matrix & 4D Tesseract SVG Inspector
window.korState = { ks: true, cs: false, km: true, cm: false };

window.toggleKorRule = function(key) {
  window.korState[key] = !window.korState[key];
  const labels = {
    ks: "K_s (Synk. Coup)",
    cs: "C_s (Synk. Comp)",
    km: "K_m (Met. Push)",
    cm: "C_m (Met. Coprod)"
  };
  let btn = document.getElementById('btn-' + key);
  if (btn) {
    if (window.korState[key]) {
      btn.style.background = (key === 'ks' || key === 'cs') ? "#20B2AA" : "#FFA500";
      btn.style.color = "#000";
      btn.style.fontWeight = "bold";
      btn.innerText = "✓ " + labels[key];
    } else {
      btn.style.background = "#1e293b";
      btn.style.color = "#FFD700";
      btn.style.fontWeight = "normal";
      btn.innerText = "✗ " + labels[key];
    }
  }
  window.updateKorMatrixStatus();
};

window.updateKorMatrixStatus = function() {
  const box = document.getElementById('kor-matrix-status');
  if (!box) return;
  let active = [];
  if (window.korState.ks) active.push("K_s");
  if (window.korState.cs) active.push("C_s");
  if (window.korState.km) active.push("K_m");
  if (window.korState.cm) active.push("C_m");

  let hasSynk = window.korState.ks || window.korState.cs;
  let hasMet = window.korState.km || window.korState.cm;
  let kappa = active.length;

  // Render 4D Tesseract 2D Projection SVG
  const svg = document.getElementById('tess-svg');
  if (svg) {
    let coords = {};
    let htmlEdges = "", htmlNodes = "";
    for (let b0 = 0; b0 <= 1; b0++) {
      for (let b1 = 0; b1 <= 1; b1++) {
        for (let b2 = 0; b2 <= 1; b2++) {
          for (let b3 = 0; b3 <= 1; b3++) {
            let scale = b3 === 1 ? 18 : 38;
            let x = 100 + (2 * b0 - 1) * scale + (2 * b2 - 1) * 12;
            let y = 68 + (2 * b1 - 1) * (scale * 0.72) - (2 * b3 - 1) * 8;
            coords[`${b0}${b1}${b2}${b3}`] = { x, y, b0, b1, b2, b3 };
          }
        }
      }
    }
    let keys = Object.keys(coords);
    for (let i = 0; i < keys.length; i++) {
      for (let j = i + 1; j < keys.length; j++) {
        let a = coords[keys[i]], b = coords[keys[j]];
        let diff = Math.abs(a.b0-b.b0) + Math.abs(a.b1-b.b1) + Math.abs(a.b2-b.b2) + Math.abs(a.b3-b.b3);
        if (diff === 1) {
          htmlEdges += `<line x1="${a.x.toFixed(1)}" y1="${a.y.toFixed(1)}" x2="${b.x.toFixed(1)}" y2="${b.y.toFixed(1)}" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.2"/>`;
        }
      }
    }
    let curKey = `${window.korState.km?1:0}${window.korState.cm?1:0}${window.korState.ks?1:0}${window.korState.cs?1:0}`;
    keys.forEach(k => {
      let c = coords[k];
      let m = (c.b0 === 1 || c.b1 === 1);
      let s = (c.b2 === 1 || c.b3 === 1);
      let col = (!m && !s) ? "#94a3b8" : (m && s ? "#20B2AA" : "#DC143C");
      let isCur = (k === curKey);
      let r = isCur ? 7.5 : 4.0;
      let stroke = isCur ? "#FFD700" : "#000";
      let sw = isCur ? 2.5 : 1.0;
      htmlNodes += `<circle cx="${c.x.toFixed(1)}" cy="${c.y.toFixed(1)}" r="${r}" fill="${isCur ? '#FFD700' : col}" stroke="${stroke}" stroke-width="${sw}"/>`;
    });
    svg.innerHTML = htmlEdges + htmlNodes;
  }

  if (kappa === 0) {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#708090";
    box.innerHTML = `<span style="color:#cbd5e1;"><b>Vacuous Origin ∅ (κ = 0):</b> No corporate rules active.</span>`;
  } else if (hasSynk && hasMet) {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#20B2AA";
    box.innerHTML = `<span style="color:#20B2AA;"><b>✓ MIXED DETERMINATE CLASS (1 of 9, Rank κ = ${kappa}):</b> r = {${active.join(", ")}}</span><br>` +
      `Satisfies Heim's <i>Eindeutigkeitssatz</i> (r ∩ Met ≠ ∅ ∧ r ∩ Synk ≠ ∅) ⇒ Unique composite Syntrix algebra S_c ∈ Obj(Syn)!`;
  } else {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#DC143C";
    let missing = hasMet ? "Synkolative module tier (K_s, C_s)" : "Metrophoric carrier tier (K_m, C_m)";
    box.innerHTML = `<span style="color:#ff6b81;"><b>✗ PURE UNDERDETERMINED CLASS (1 of 6, Rank κ = ${kappa}):</b> r = {${active.join(", ")}}</span><br>` +
      `Violates <i>Eindeutigkeitssatz</i>: leaves the ${missing} underdetermined (*zweideutig*)!`;
  }
};

// WIDGET 5: §3.3.4 Homogeneous Decomposition & Compositive Population Balance
window.updateDecompLab = function() {
  const elStep = document.getElementById('dec-step');
  if (!elStep) return;
  let k = parseInt(elStep.value);
  let nH = parseInt(document.getElementById('dec-nh').value);
  let mu = parseInt(document.getElementById('dec-mu').value);

  document.getElementById('dec-step-val').innerText = `k = ${k}`;
  document.getElementById('dec-nh-val').innerText = nH;
  document.getElementById('dec-mu-val').innerText = mu;

  let remMu = Math.max(0, 4 - k);
  let pyrSum = Math.max(0, nH - mu);
  let p1 = Math.floor(pyrSum * 0.45), p2 = Math.floor(pyrSum * 0.35), p3 = pyrSum - p1 - p2;

  let stages = [
    { lbl: "x yã (μ=4)", active: k === 0, col: "#9370DB" },
    { lbl: "D_s¹ (μ=3)", active: k === 1, col: "#FFA500" },
    { lbl: "D_s² (μ=2)", active: k === 2, col: "#20B2AA" },
    { lbl: "D_s³ (μ=1)", active: k === 3, col: "#4169E1" },
    { lbl: "0_Syn (μ=0)", active: k === 4, col: "#DC143C" }
  ];
  document.getElementById('dec-chain-cards').innerHTML = stages.map(s => `
    <div style="flex:1; text-align:center; padding:5px; border-radius:5px; font-size:0.58em; font-weight:bold;
         background:${s.active ? s.col : '#151c2c'}; color:${s.active ? '#000' : '#94a3b8'}; border:1px solid ${s.col};">
      ${s.lbl}
    </div>
  `).join("");

  const box = document.getElementById('dec-readout');
  if (box) {
    box.style.borderLeftColor = remMu === 0 ? "#FFD700" : "#20B2AA";
    box.innerHTML =
      `<b>Complexity μ(D_s^${k}(S)) = ${remMu}:</b> ${remMu === 0 ? '<span style="color:#FFD700;">TERMINATED AT NULLSYNTRIX 0_Syn!</span>' : 'Contracting historical cross-talk into pyramidal components...'}<br>` +
      `<b>Thm. 3.10 Additive Population Balance:</b> n_H - μ = ${nH} - ${mu} = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${pyrSum}</b> = ∑ n_j (${p1} + ${p2} + ${p3})`;
  }
};

// WIDGET 6 & 7: §3.3.5 Syntropod Tree, Forest Surgery & Pseudoexzenter Fan-Out
window.treeEdgesEx = [true, false, true];
window.surgeryMode = false;

window.toggleTreeEdge = function(idx) {
  window.treeEdgesEx[idx] = !window.treeEdgesEx[idx];
  window.renderSyntropodTree();
};

window.toggleForestSurgery = function() {
  window.surgeryMode = !window.surgeryMode;
  window.renderSyntropodTree();
};

window.renderSyntropodTree = function() {
  const elFan = document.getElementById('fan-n');
  if (!elFan) return;
  let N = parseInt(elFan.value);
  document.getElementById('fan-n-val').innerText = N;
  let fanBranches = (N * (N + 1)) / 2;

  const configs = [
    { nd: 'nd-kor1', tx: 'tx-kor1', l1: 'te-1a', l2: 'te-1b', name: 'Kor₁' },
    { nd: 'nd-kor2', tx: 'tx-kor2', l1: 'te-2a', l2: 'te-2b', name: 'Kor₂' },
    { nd: 'nd-kor3', tx: 'tx-kor3', l1: 'te-3a', l2: 'te-3b', name: 'Apex Kor₃' }
  ];
  let eps = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    let isEx = window.treeEdgesEx[i];
    if (isEx) eps++;
    let c = configs[i];
    let rect = document.getElementById(c.nd);
    let txt = document.getElementById(c.tx);
    let lineA = document.getElementById(c.l1);
    let lineB = document.getElementById(c.l2);

    if (isEx) {
      rect.setAttribute('stroke', '#FFA500');
      rect.setAttribute('fill', '#2d1a04');
      txt.setAttribute('fill', '#FFA500');
      txt.textContent = `${c.name}: Exzenter (K_m)`;
      lineA.setAttribute('stroke', '#FFA500');
      lineB.setAttribute('stroke', '#FFA500');
      lineA.setAttribute('opacity', window.surgeryMode ? '0.12' : '1.0');
      lineB.setAttribute('opacity', window.surgeryMode ? '0.12' : '1.0');
    } else {
      rect.setAttribute('stroke', '#4169E1');
      rect.setAttribute('fill', '#0f1b3d');
      txt.setAttribute('fill', '#82aaff');
      txt.textContent = `${c.name}: Konzenter (C_m)`;
      lineA.setAttribute('stroke', '#4169E1');
      lineB.setAttribute('stroke', '#4169E1');
      lineA.setAttribute('opacity', '1.0');
      lineB.setAttribute('opacity', '1.0');
    }
  }
  let kc = 3 - eps;
  let confIdx = eps + 1;
  let status = document.getElementById('tree-readout');
  status.innerHTML =
    `<b>Conflexivity:</b> |E_K|=ε=<b>${eps}</b>, |E_C|=<b>${kc}</b> ⇒ <b>ConfIndex_pres = ε + 1 = ${confIdx}</b>` +
    (window.surgeryMode ? ` <span style="color:#20B2AA;">[Forest Surgery: ${confIdx} Subtrees]</span>` : '') +
    `  |  <b>Thm. 3.11 (N=${N}):</b> ½N(N+1) = <b style="color:#FFD700;">${fanBranches} Branches</b>`;
};

// WIDGET 8: §3.3.6 Mayer-Vietoris Homological Emergence
window.updateMayerVietoris = function() {
  const elG = document.getElementById('mv-glue');
  if (!elG) return;
  let g = parseInt(elG.value);
  document.getElementById('mv-glue-val').innerText = g + '%';
  let t = g / 100.0;

  let yTop = 35 + t * 30.0;
  let yBot = 95 - t * 30.0;
  document.getElementById('mv-arc-top').setAttribute('d', `M 90,${yTop} Q 210,${-10 + t*20} 330,${yTop}`);
  document.getElementById('mv-arc-bot').setAttribute('d', `M 90,${yBot} Q 210,${140 - t*20} 330,${yBot}`);
  document.getElementById('mv-v0').setAttribute('cy', yTop);
  document.getElementById('mv-v1').setAttribute('cy', yTop);
  document.getElementById('mv-w0').setAttribute('cy', yBot);
  document.getElementById('mv-w1').setAttribute('cy', yBot);

  let cycTxt = document.getElementById('mv-cycle-txt');
  let box = document.getElementById('mv-readout');
  if (g >= 96) {
    cycTxt.setAttribute('opacity', '1');
    document.getElementById('mv-arc-top').setAttribute('stroke', '#FFD700');
    document.getElementById('mv-arc-bot').setAttribute('stroke', '#FFD700');
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#FFD700";
    box.innerHTML = `<span style="color:#FFD700;"><b>✓ HOMOLOGICAL FUSION EMERGENCE (v_i = w_i):</b> H₁(S_c) ≅ ker(δ_{φ*}) ≅ ℝ[e_a - e_b] ≠ 0!</span>`;
  } else {
    cycTxt.setAttribute('opacity', '0');
    document.getElementById('mv-arc-top').setAttribute('stroke', '#4169E1');
    document.getElementById('mv-arc-bot').setAttribute('stroke', '#20B2AA');
    box.style.borderLeftColor = "#20B2AA";
    box.innerHTML = `Uncoupled / Partial Gluing (${g}%): Boundaries separate ⇒ H₁(S_a) = 0, H₁(S_b) = 0 (No global cycle).`;
  }
};

function ensureVideosPlaying() {
  document.querySelectorAll('video').forEach(v => {
    v.muted = true;
    v.playsInline = true;
    if (v.paused) v.play().catch(() => {});
  });
}

function initAllCh3Widgets() {
  window.updateMetCorp();
  window.updatePushoutLab();
  window.updateKonflektorLab();
  window.updateKorMatrixStatus();
  window.updateDecompLab();
  window.renderSyntropodTree();
  window.updateMayerVietoris();
  ensureVideosPlaying();

  document.querySelectorAll('input[type="range"], select, button').forEach(input => {
    input.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
    input.addEventListener('mousedown', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
    input.addEventListener('touchstart', (e) => e.stopPropagation(), {passive: true});
  });

  if ('IntersectionObserver' in window) {
    const obs = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
      entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting && entry.target.tagName === 'VIDEO') {
          entry.target.muted = true;
          entry.target.play().catch(() => {});
        }
      });
    }, { threshold: 0.15 });
    document.querySelectorAll('video').forEach(v => obs.observe(v));
  }
}

if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", initAllCh3Widgets);
} else {
  initAllCh3Widgets();
}

window.addEventListener('load', initAllCh3Widgets);
if (window.Reveal) {
  window.Reveal.on('ready', initAllCh3Widgets);
  window.Reveal.on('slidechanged', initAllCh3Widgets);
}
</script>
